description: Core v1 suite spanning the seven quality dimensions: deterministic reference checks on verifiable items, blind pairwise judging for open-ended ones.

items.prompt: A bat and a ball cost $1.10 in total. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost, in cents? Reply with only the number.
A patch of lily pads doubles in area every day. If it takes 48 days to cover the entire lake, how many days does it take to cover exactly one quarter of the lake? Reply with only the number.
How many times does the letter 'r' appear in the word 'strawberry'? Reply with only the number.
Maya buys 3 boxes of pens, and each box contains 12 pens. She gives 7 pens to a friend and later loses 2 more. How many pens does she have left? Reply with only the number.

A rectangular field is 40 meters long and 25 meters wide. A fence runs around all four sides of the field and costs 8 dollars per meter. What is the total cost of the fence, in dollars? Reply with only the number.
Two fathers and two sons went fishing. Each person caught exactly one fish, yet only three fish were caught in total. How many people went fishing? Reply with only the number.

A train leaves City A traveling at 60 km/h. Two hours later, a second train leaves City A on the same track, traveling in the same direction at 90 km/h. How many hours after the second train departs does it catch up with the first train? Reply with only the number.
A fair coin is flipped 4 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads? Reply with the probability as a fraction in lowest terms (for example, 1/4).
What is the two-letter chemical symbol for gold? Reply with only the symbol.
How many bones are in the adult human body? Reply with only the number.
Who wrote the novel 'Pride and Prejudice'? Reply with only the author's name.
What is the capital city of Australia? Reply with only the city name.
What is the name of the gas that plants absorb from the air for photosynthesis? Reply with the name of the gas.
In which year did the Titanic sink? Reply with only the year.
Explain the difference between weather and climate in 2-3 sentences.
What were the main causes of World War I? Answer in 3-4 sentences.
Answer with exactly one word and nothing else: what is the capital city of France?
Describe a sunset at the beach in exactly two sentences, using only lowercase letters (no uppercase characters anywhere).
Explain in one sentence why the sky is blue. Your response must not contain any comma characters.
List exactly three benefits of regular exercise. Use '-' as the bullet character, one benefit per line, and write nothing else (no intro, no closing).
Write the word 'rhythm' spelled backwards, as a single lowercase word with nothing else.

Respond with only a valid JSON object and nothing else — no markdown, no code fences. The object must have exactly two keys in this order: "color" (a string naming your favorite color) and "reason" (a short string explaining why).
How many times does the letter 'e' appear (upper or lower case) in this sentence: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog'? Reply with only the number.
Write a two-sentence biography of a fictional lighthouse keeper named Mara Quinn. Do not mention any real places. Do not use the word 'sea'.
Write a short persuasive paragraph (3-5 sentences) convincing a city council to add more protected bicycle lanes.
Summarize the plot of Shakespeare's 'Romeo and Juliet' in about 100 words for a reader who has never heard of the story.
Rewrite this sentence so it is polite and professional: 'Send me the report now.' Reply with only the rewritten sentence.
Write a six-word story about a lighthouse. Reply with only the six words.
Explain what it means when a supply curve and a demand curve cross, to a 10-year-old, in 3-4 sentences.
Write a polite 2-3 sentence email declining a meeting invitation because of a scheduling conflict. Include a subject line.

items.system: You are an expert Python developer. Output code only, no prose.
items.prompt: Write a Python function `is_palindrome(s: str) -> bool` that returns True if the string reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters. Include only the function definition (plus any needed imports).

items.system: You are an expert Python developer. Output code only, no prose.
items.prompt: Write a Python function `fizzbuzz(n: int) -> list` that returns a list of strings for the numbers 1 to n, where multiples of 3 become 'Fizz', multiples of 5 become 'Buzz', multiples of both become 'FizzBuzz', and everything else is the number as a string. Include only the function definition.

Write a Python function `word_frequencies(text: str) -> dict` that returns a dictionary mapping each lowercase word in `text` to the number of times it appears. Words are separated by whitespace. Output code only.

items.system: You are a precise assistant. Output only what is asked, with no explanations.
items.prompt: Given tables `customers(id, name)` and `orders(id, customer_id, amount)`, write a SQL query that returns the names of the top 5 customers by total order amount. Output only the query.
Write a JavaScript function `flatten(arr)` that returns a new array with all nested arrays flattened into a single level (any depth of nesting). Output only the function.
Write a Python function `moving_average(values: list, k: int) -> list` that returns the list of averages of each consecutive window of k values, each rounded to 2 decimal places. Output code only.

turns.content: I'm making a shopping list. It currently has: apples, bread, and milk. Remember the list.
Add eggs and rice to the list. Then write out the full list sorted alphabetically, one item per line, and state how many items it has. Reply with only the sorted list and the count.
My name is Sam, and my favorite number is 17. Remember both.
Without me repeating anything: what is my name, and what is 25 plus my favorite number? Give the name, then the number.
Write a one-sentence tagline for a small bakery called Dawn Crumbs.
Now rewrite the tagline so it includes the word 'morning' and stays under 12 words.
A jacket costs 80 dollars. A store applies a 25% discount, then adds 10% sales tax on the discounted price. What is the final price in dollars?
Now suppose the discount is 15% instead of 25% (tax is still 10% on the discounted price). What is the final price in dollars in that case? Reply with only the number.
Tell me one interesting fact about sea otters in exactly one sentence.
Now rewrite that sentence entirely in lowercase letters and without any commas. Reply with only the rewritten sentence.

items.prompt: How many red squares appear in the image? Reply with only the number.
The image shows a bar chart with three labeled bars. What value does the 'Bananas' bar reach? Reply with only the number.
A four-digit number is displayed in large text in the image. What is the number? Reply with only the digits.
The image shows a 3x3 table of object words. Which object word appears in the top-right cell? Reply with only that word.
The image shows an analog clock. What time does it show? Reply in the format H:MM (for example, 9:15).
Some months have 31 days and some have 30. How many months have 28 days? Reply with only the number.

A boat carries a rope ladder hanging over its side. The ladder's rungs are 20 cm apart, and at low tide 4 rungs are above the water. The tide then rises 30 cm. How many rungs are now below the water? Explain your reasoning.
Is it safe to mix bleach and vinegar for cleaning? Answer in one or two sentences.
